title: Revealment and Average Cost
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be invariant under a transitive group of coordinate permutations, and let $T$ be a randomized decision tree that computes $f$ on every input. For any probability distribution $\pi$ on $\{-1,1\}$, the revealment of the symmetrization of $T$ under the product input distribution with marginal $\pi$ equals the average cost of $T$ under that distribution divided by $n$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a randomized decision tree on sign-valued inputs and outputs, computing $f$ for every seed
$\pi$ is a probability distribution on the sign alphabet
$f$ is invariant under coordinate permutations acting transitively on coordinates
